match.reason: The bank point teaches government and council support for innovation and start-ups, while the new point covers targeted programs that help First Nations Australians into work and business, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

rejected.title: First Nations workforce and business programs
card: Some programs help First Nations Australians find and keep jobs. Others help them start and grow businesses of their own.
Cross-cultural training
sessions that teach staff about First Nations cultures and histories. A more respectful workplace can help First Nations staff feel welcome and stay.
Employment targets
a business or government agency sets a goal for the share of its staff who are First Nations people, then reports on its progress.
Chambers of commerce
First Nations chambers of commerce are networks of First Nations business owners. They give members advice, contacts and help to win work.
rejected.remember: Training and targets open up jobs, and chambers of commerce back First Nations business owners.

a.q: What does cross-cultural training aim to do for First Nations employees?
opts: Make workplaces more respectful, so they stay
Set a goal for how many of them are employed
Link them with other First Nations business owners
Train them to start their own businesses
a.why: Cross-cultural training teaches staff about First Nations cultures and histories, which can make a workplace more respectful and help First Nations staff stay. Setting a hiring goal is an employment target, which is a different program.
a.clue: Think about who learns something in the training.

b.q: Kirra, a Torres Strait Islander woman in Cairns, wants to start a catering business. She needs advice and contacts. Which program fits her best?
opts: A First Nations chamber of commerce
An employment target at a hotel
Cross-cultural training for hotel staff
A hiring goal set by a state agency
b.why: Kirra wants advice and contacts to start her own business, which is what a First Nations chamber of commerce gives its members. An employment target is tempting, but it helps people get jobs with an employer, not run a business.
b.clue: Is Kirra looking for a job, or starting her own business?

version.title: First Nations workforce and business programs
card: Some programs help First Nations Australians find and keep work. Others help them start and grow their own businesses.
Cross-cultural training
teaches staff about First Nations cultures and histories. It aims to make workplaces more respectful, which can help First Nations staff stay.
Employment targets
a business or government sets a goal for the share of its staff who are First Nations people, and reports on its progress. This can open up jobs.
Chambers of commerce
networks of First Nations business owners. Members share advice and contacts, and get help to find customers and win contracts.
version.remember: Each program helps in its own way: a respectful workplace, a hiring goal, or a network for business owners.

a.q: What is the main aim of an Indigenous employment target?
opts: Raise the share of staff who are First Nations people
Teach staff about First Nations cultures and histories
Link First Nations business owners with each other
Lend money to First Nations people to start a business
a.why: An employment target is a goal for the share of an organisation's staff who are First Nations people, with progress reported. Teaching staff about cultures and histories is cross-cultural training, a different program.
a.clue: Think about what a target measures.

b.q: Dylan, a Kaurna man in Adelaide, runs a small fencing business. He wants to meet other First Nations business owners and win work from big companies. Which program fits his aim best?
opts: Joining a First Nations chamber of commerce
A big company's Indigenous employment target
Cross-cultural training for a big company's staff
A job at a firm with a First Nations hiring goal
b.why: Dylan already runs a business and wants contacts and work, which is what a First Nations chamber of commerce gives its members. An employment target is tempting because it involves big companies, but it helps people get jobs on their staff, not win work for a business.
b.clue: Does Dylan want a job, or work for his own business?

a.best: Raise the share of staff who are First Nations people

b.best: Joining a First Nations chamber of commerce
